# Lab 18.5: Create a Confidential VM

## What We Are Going to Do
Create a Confidential VM with AMD SEV, check from inside that memory encryption is on, and find the attestation report.

## Steps

1. **Create the VM.** Confidential VMs need supported machine types and must stop for host maintenance.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud compute instances create cvm-lab \
  --zone=us-central1-a \
  --machine-type=n2d-standard-2 \
  --confidential-compute-type=SEV \
  --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE \
  --shielded-secure-boot \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2404-lts-amd64 \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **Check it in the console.** Open the VM details. **Confidential VM service** shows **Enabled** with type **AMD SEV**.

3. **Check from inside.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud compute ssh cvm-lab --zone=us-central1-a --command="sudo dmesg | grep -i sev"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   You see `Memory Encryption Features active: AMD SEV`.

4. **Find the launch attestation.** In **Logs Explorer**, run:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • TEXT
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">resource.type="gce_instance"
jsonPayload.@type="type.googleapis.com/cloud_integrity.IntegrityEvent"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Look for `sevLaunchAttestationReportEvent`.

5. **Other options.** `--confidential-compute-type=SEV_SNP` adds memory integrity. `TDX` uses Intel machines such as `c3-standard-4`. Supported zones differ, so check the docs.

6. **Require it.** In **Organization policies**, look at **Restrict Non-Confidential Computing** (`compute.restrictNonConfidentialComputing`).

7. **Clean up.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud compute instances delete cvm-lab --zone=us-central1-a --quiet</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Memory | Encrypted by the AMD CPU |
| Guest OS check | `dmesg` shows SEV active |
| Attestation | Launch report in Cloud Logging |
| Code changes | None |
